title: Governance doctrine — agents that cannot hurt you
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: This is Softanza's signature — the one capability where, in the platform survey, it out-covers .NET, Python, Wolfram and the JVM alike. The doctrine is that safety is architectural, not procedural: an LLM (or any untrusted capability) cannot act effectfully by construction — it holds only the `inference` capability, granting it `effectful` raises at construction, and effectful work rehearses in a semantic virtual world whose only export is a reviewable update plan a governed actor commits. One rule gate then judges the result across eleven domains. And the field is moving the other way — Java's `SecurityManager` is deprecated, .NET's Code Access Security was removed — so Softanza builds in what the platforms are retiring.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: A cross-cutting doctrine measured against how the field handles safe, governed execution — policy engines (OPA/Rego), sandboxes (seccomp, gVisor, Deno), object-capability systems, AI-agent guardrails (Guardrails, NeMo), and secrets/identity (Vault, SPIFFE). The split is clean: the architecture is distinctive and guarded; the closure (a formal capability type, the negotiation loop) is the frontier.

lanes.engine: `stzAgentGraph` gives every actor a capability set and a taint colour. `AddLLMActor` grants `["inference"]` only — the effect set is empty — and `Grant(llm,"effectful")` raises: "an LLM proposes, only a pi-gate commits — enforced at CONSTRUCTION, not merely audited."
lanes.owed: The refusal is structural, not a runtime policy check. The effect capability simply isn't in the LLM actor's set to begin with — closer to object-capability discipline than to a prompt-level or stack-walk guard. Guard: `agentgraph_narrated`.

lanes.lane: The safe world — rehearse → plan → commit
lanes.engine: `stzVirtualSystem` + `stzVirtualFileSystem` are a real in-memory twin (tree state, snapshots, branches, tombstones). Effectful work runs against the twin; the tick's only export is a reviewable `stzUpdatePlan`. Principle P1: "the virtual layer holds no reference to reality."
lanes.owed: Unlike a container you can only throw away, the plan is a reviewable, rejectable artifact — a semantic sandbox that speaks files and operations, not opaque syscalls. Guard: `safeworld_narrated` (76/76).

lanes.engine: `stzUpdatePlan.Execute()` passes every operation through three gates — reviewer, commit scope (`stzCommitScope`), and capability (`executor.Can(RequiredKind())`). `MayCommit()` answers "this LLM's plan cannot cross" before any attempt; the lattice (`effectful/sensing/compute/inference`) refuses an unknown kind.
lanes.owed: The gates compose — an LLM is refused even inside an allowing scope, and a human can commit the very same plan. One crossing point between imagination and reality. Guard: `governance_crossing_narrated` (Scene 10).

lanes.engine: `stzRuleReport` collects findings in one shape `[:rule,:subject,:where,:severity,:message]` with `IsSound()`, from 11 self-checking domains (code, security, agent, org, service, ER, petri, network, fault, family, diagram); `stzPredicateSet` is the signable, sha256-sealed constitution.
lanes.owed: One gate spanning code and agents and services and security and diagram models — broader than any single policy engine's remit (each is single-domain). The governance verdict has one address.

lanes.engine: OS effects — `create_file`, `set_var`, `spawn_process`, `change_dir` — are `stzVirtualOperation`s requiring the `effectful` capability; they reach reality only through the update plan, which refuses any executor lacking the kind or a declared trust posture. `stzVirtualEnvironment` extends the twin to env vars and cwd.
lanes.owed: The doctrine applied to the OS surface — real and guarded (`governance_crossing`, env twin) — but a focused effect set (files / env / process), not yet the whole syscall surface.

lanes.engine: `stzSecretStore` is enumerable and all reads self-redact; `Reveal(name, actor)` is gated to an effectful, non-sandboxed actor, so an inference-only LLM cannot reveal a secret. Refusals are recorded as security events — the secret name only, never the value. `stzVaultResolver` bridges external stores.
lanes.owed: The secret gate is the same lattice as the effect gate — one capability model, not a bolt-on keyring. Vault-grade discipline built into the doctrine. Guard: `secretstore_narrated`.

lanes.engine: `stzSecurityLedger` is append-only and hash-chained (`Verify()` names the first broken link); `SealTo(path,key)` is a keyed HMAC-SHA256 export, and a Ring copy records into the same evidence. It is honest about its threat model: it detects retroactive edits, but an in-process attacker can still append or wipe.
lanes.owed: Tamper-evidence with a stated, honest threat model — strong on retroactive edits, explicit that it is not append-proof against an in-process attacker. Guard: `security_ledger_narrated` (10 scenes).

lanes.engine: `stzServiceRegistry` asks each service its posture — `:sandbox` (a fake, must-not-ship), `:local`, `:live`. `SetPhase(:production)` raises an ERROR `sandbox-in-production` and `ephemeral-in-production` (a sqlite `":memory:"` — one character from the safe spelling); `stzServiceRule` answers, in development, which part depends on a fake.
lanes.owed: A fake reaching production is refused by construction, not by discipline — and the sandboxes are genuine (a real P-256 key), so "we tested against the sandbox" means something. Guard: `service_registry_narrated`.

lanes.engine: A broad shipped surface (23 files in `base/security`): auth (`stzAuth`, OIDC, SAML, passkey, TOTP, request signer) plus `stzSecurityPosture` / Attestation / Drill / Sentinel / Detection / Incident / ResponsePlan, with `stzSecurityGraph` self-checking via `CheckRules()` into the same rule gate.
lanes.owed: A comprehensive identity + posture layer feeding the one gate — broad and real, though it composes existing protocols (OIDC/SAML/passkey) rather than inventing them. The doctrine's perimeter, not its novelty.

lanes.lane: Governance as a file — the `.pia` agent
lanes.engine: `stzAgentDeclaration` compiles a `.pia` declarative agent to the same classes and quotes `stzAgentGraph.Grant`'s refusal verbatim — "one rule, two doors, same words." A `pia: 2` posture requirement refuses a `ring:` clause with no declared posture. An agent is a file judged at load.
lanes.owed: The doctrine reachable declaratively, not only in code — a distinctive "constitution as a file." The v1 files remain readable as a stated migration debt (lane 12).

lanes.engine: The plan now reaches the agent (`stzAgentWorkbench` + `GiveWorkbench`, shipped 2026-08-22), but the conversation about the plan is design-only: `Receive(issues)` / `Revise()`, `stzAgentEvaluation` (the "examination hall"), and branch-per-hypothesis (`BranchFrom` / `CompareBranches` exist on the vfs but no agent uses them).
lanes.owed: The doc's own words: "the plan reaches the agent; the conversation about the plan does not yet." Build Receive/Revise, the evaluation hall, and branch-per-hypothesis into a real agent. `stzHybridAgent` is named but never built as a class.

lanes.engine: The by-construction guarantees are real at the `Grant` boundary and the plan crossing; where they aren't, an audit (`Violations()`) is the acknowledged backstop — "by construction" becoming "by detection" at the edges.
lanes.owed: Three honest holes: no formal capability type (kinds are strings in list properties, and a raw `SetNodeProperty` bypasses `Grant`); the registration gate is opt-in (a migration default until the last in-tree host declares); the `ring:` escape checks the function name, not what it does (backstopped by posture + reversibility, not closed).

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The architecture is strong; the gaps are closure and depth — the first tier makes the guarantee airtight, the second finishes the wiring, the third builds the loop that lets an agent argue with its own rejected plan.

tiers.title: Tier A — make the guarantee airtight

items.title: A formal capability type
items.text: Capabilities are string kinds in list properties, so a raw `SetNodeProperty` can still grant an effect around `Grant` — the `Violations()` audit catches it after the fact. A real capability type that cannot be forged would turn the last "by detection" edges into "by construction."

items.title: Flip the registration gate to default
items.text: The engine-loop registration gate (`MayRegister`) is opt-in (`UseEngineLoop()`); the default only flips when the last in-tree host declares. Wire `appserver/`, `cluster/` and `perf/` to declare, and the migration state becomes the guarantee.

items.title: Close the `ring:` escape
items.text: The `ring:` clause is checked by function name, not by what the function does — closed today only by the `pia: 2` posture requirement composed against reversibility. Make the check behavioral (or run the body itself in the twin) so a mislabeled function can't slip an effect through.

items.title: Wire the native roster
items.text: `stzOwnAgentStack` declares five library-internal agents and wires one (`wise-coder`); the other four raise if asked. Finishing them turns the "self-governing library" from a demonstrated pattern into a live one.

tiers.title: Tier C — build the conversation about the plan

items.title: The negotiation loop
items.text: Ship `Receive(issues)` / `Revise()` so a rejected plan comes back to the agent with the reviewer's findings, and the agent proposes again — the missing half of propose-review-commit. The plan reaches the agent; the argument about it should too.

items.title: The evaluation hall & branches
items.text: Wire `stzAgentEvaluation` and branch-per-hypothesis (the vfs already has `BranchFrom` / `CompareBranches`) so an agent can rehearse several plans and a governed actor picks the winner — rehearsal as comparison, not just as a single dry run.

items.title: Build `stzHybridAgent`
items.text: `AddHybridActor` is only a graph node and colour — a composition proven sound that instantiates nothing. Building it as a real class would let one actor hold both proposing and (scoped) committing roles under the same lattice.

notes.text: "We will not build safe agents. We will build a safe world, and let ordinary agents loose inside it. The workbench holds no reference to reality."

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: This page rates a cross-cutting doctrine, not a module — it lives across `base/agentic`, `base/system`, `base/security`, `base/service` and `base/graph`. Read from `main`. The strengths are real and guarded: `Grant` refuses at construction; the safe-world twin exports a reviewable plan; `MayCommit` refuses the LLM before it tries; the 11-domain rule gate; production refuses fakes; the hash-chained ledger; capability-gated secrets. The weaknesses are equally on the page, and the design doc grades itself this candidly (`SOFTANZA_INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §3.1–3.2): the negotiation loop and `stzHybridAgent` are design-only, the registration gate is opt-in, and there is no formal capability type — the audit is where "by construction" becomes "by detection."

Softanza is the only stack in the mainstream field that makes safe execution architectural rather than procedural — the LLM cannot act because it never holds the capability, effectful work rehearses in a reviewable world, and one gate judges the result across every domain; what it still owes is the airtight type behind the discipline and the negotiation loop that lets an agent argue with its own rejected plan.
